caption: A promotional poster features a soccer theme with a large action photo of a male player in a light blue jersey and black shorts performing a high kick in a brightly lit stadium. The right half has a blue gradient background with the citi logo at the top. White text reads “Celebrate the game with Coca‑Cola” and advertises up to 18.3% fuel savings and exclusive gifts at Esso. A panel shows two monthly offers: April—free Coca‑Cola 4‑slim‑can pack, and May—free six Coca‑Cola contour glasses, earned by spending S$60 or more on fuel with a Citibank credit/debit card. Images of the can pack and glasses appear, along with small pictures of several Citibank cards. Logos for Coca‑Cola, Cheers, FairPrice Xpress, and Esso line the bottom, above detailed terms and conditions.

The image shows a close-up of a person’s lower legs and feet standing on a pale green background. Around the ankles is a large, yellow paper crown with multiple Burger King logos, appearing oversized like a cuff. The person wears shiny red peep-toe heels, and their skin is light. The crown’s design features a sunburst pattern and rounded points. In the lower right corner, there is a small photograph of a salad in a black bowl with visible ingredients such as lettuce, tomato slices, croutons or cheese cubes, and grilled chicken pieces. Next to the salad is colorful text reading “check our new chicken salads.” The overall style is clean and minimal with soft lighting.

The image is an advertising poster for Dunkin’ Donuts titled “Flavor Radio!” promoting a special radio advertisement that releases a coffee aroma using sound recognition. At the top left is the Dunkin’ Donuts logo. The poster explains a mission to increase the coffee consumer base in Seoul. A diagram shows steps: a bus plays a DD radio ad, a sound recognition machine detects the jingle, an atomizer releases coffee aroma, people notice it, and they visit a Dunkin’ Donuts shop. A device resembling an automatic sprayer is pictured. A results panel shows icons with “Visitors increased 16%” and “Sales increased 29%.” Photos at the bottom include a steaming Dunkin’ coffee cup and small images of buses, equipment, stores, and smiling customers.

A vibrant advertising image features a red background with black vine-like shapes and faint outdoor-themed icons. On the left, bold yellow text reads “A Taste That Inspires.” Beneath it are three checklist items with black check marks: “New Trail,” “New Gear,” and “New Salad.” A person wearing running gear, seen from behind, runs along a stylized path toward the right. On the right, a large bowl of salad is prominently displayed, filled with greens, corn, black beans, grilled chicken strips, cheese, tortilla strips, and lime wedges. Decorative elements include silhouettes of a bird, a flower, a pocket watch, and activity symbols. At the bottom right, small text says “The New Southwest Salad” beside the McDonald’s logo and slogan.

The image shows a polished advertisement-style scene featuring three blue Pepsi cans standing on a glossy, dark blue background. The center can faces forward with the red, white, and blue Pepsi globe logo and vertical “pepsi” text visible; the two cans behind it are slightly turned and partly obscured. Dynamic splashes of clear water arc around the cans, with droplets scattered in the air and reflections faintly visible on the surface below. Each can appears to be 12 fl oz, indicated near the lower edge. At the bottom center of the image, the slogan “REFRESH YOUR WORLD pepsi” appears in small white lettering. No people are present.

The image is a minimalist advertisement featuring a tilted plastic bottle labeled “ethos. WATER” pouring light blue water that splashes into a heart shape against a white background. In the top right corner is a small green circular logo with a crowned figure, associated with a coffee brand. The bottle is partially cropped on the left side, with its cap removed and liquid streaming out in droplets and a curved flow. At the bottom, bold black text reads, “Your sip, their survival.” Below it is smaller paragraph text explaining that more than 800 million people worldwide lack clean water and that purchasing a bottle contributes five cents to the Ethos Water Fund through local Starbucks. No people appear in the image.

A Coca‑Cola advertisement features a clean white background with the red Coca‑Cola logo and the phrase “open happiness” in the top right corner. On the right, two hands hold and clink chilled Coca‑Cola bottles with condensation and ice inside; each bottle has a red label printed with large white names: “Kylie” on the left bottle and “Luke” on the right bottle. Small droplets and splashes appear near the bottle mouths, suggesting they were just bumped together. On the left, bold black text reads “Share a Coke with a friend,” with “Coke” in red. Below, smaller text invites getting in touch with friends and shows the website “shareacoke.com.au.” The background fades from white to very pale blue.

The image shows a minimalist advertisement with a white background. At the center-right, a wedge of pale yellow cheese stands upright next to a bright red tomato with a green stem. To the left of the food items, small green text explains that Dunkin Donuts is offering more than morning donuts and now has personal pizzas available whenever wanted. Near the bottom center, the Dunkin’ Donuts logo appears with the phrase “more than coffee and donuts.” A thin line of fine print runs along the very bottom, listing participating states. There are no people present, and the composition emphasizes the fresh ingredients and the clean, spacious layout.

A promotional graphic features the McDonald’s golden arches behind bold text reading “The Historical Timeline of the McDonald’s Menu in the USA.” In the foreground, a row of menu items is displayed on a light, striped background. From left to right are a granola-topped yogurt parfait in a clear cup, several breaded chicken pieces, a McRib-style sandwich, a sesame-seed bun burger resembling a Big Mac, a Filet-O-Fish with cheese on a plain bun, a fresh green salad in a black bowl, a breakfast wrap with visible eggs and sausage, and two red cartons of French fries in different sizes. Faint vertical labels of other menu names appear in the background as subtle text. No people are visible.

A yellow-toned Burger King advertisement features bold red-brown text at the top reading “COME BACK and SHAKE UP YOUR WAKE UP.” The Burger King logo appears in the upper-right corner. Center-left is a black plastic bowl filled with a breakfast mix of scrambled eggs, diced potatoes, peppers, and melted cheese, shown in close-up. In front of the bowl is an English muffin sandwich with a sausage patty, egg, and slice of cheese. Large labels read “New BK Breakfast Bowl” and “New BK Breakfast Muffin Sandwich.” Fine print at the bottom notes price and participation may vary and that the items are available during breakfast hours only. No people are visible.

A bright blue background features a single chilled soda can positioned on the right. The can is dark blue with water droplets and condensation, suggesting it is cold. Prominently displayed on the can is the circular red, white, and blue Pepsi logo, with the word “pepsi” printed vertically in white near the bottom. To the left, large bold white text tilted diagonally reads “REFRESH YOUR WORLD.” The can has a silver rim and base, with subtle reflections and shadows on the surface and on the ground beneath it. No people are present; the composition is clean, graphic, and product-focused, emphasizing the beverage and the slogan.

A white takeaway coffee cup with a green circular logo sits on a wooden table in the left foreground. The cup has a white plastic lid and a column of small check boxes printed on one side. The background is warmly lit and heavily blurred, suggesting an indoor setting with golden tones and indistinct shapes. On the right side, large bold white text reads “The best coffee For the best YOU.” with “YOU.” in dark green. Below that, a cursive line of text says “Taste of Inspiration.” The overall composition emphasizes the cup and the promotional message, with no visible people present.

A bright red Coca‑Cola advertisement shows a smiling man and woman sitting close together, each holding a classic glass Coca‑Cola bottle with the logo visible. They lean toward each other and laugh, suggesting a friendly moment. White illustrated bubbles float upward across the red background. Large white text on the right reads “happiness. coca-cola.” In the top right corner is a circular Coca‑Cola logo and the hashtag “#openhappiness.” At the bottom right is a QR code with small instructions nearby. The man wears a gray shirt with a red collar accent and a watch, while the woman wears a plaid shirt. The overall design is clean, bright, and centered on the beverage brand.

The image shows a stylized advertisement centered on a transparent, glasslike hamburger composed of two rounded bun shapes with water inside. A small orange goldfish swims within the upper water-filled section, while the middle layer appears to be a slab of clear ice or another glass element suggesting a sandwich filling. The background is a smooth gradient of light blue to teal. At the top center, bold white text reads “Filet-O-Fish®.” In the bottom right corner, a red square contains the yellow McDonald’s Golden Arches logo with the slogan “i’m lovin’ it.” No people are present, and the overall look is clean, glossy, and minimalistic.

The image is a minimalist advertisement with a pale green background. Large white text in the upper left reads, “MAKES OTHER SNACKS LOOK SCARY.” At center is a sculpture arranged from orange cheese-puff snacks shaped to resemble a spider with a round body and eight legs casting soft shadows. In the lower right corner sits a plastic cup of a yellow smoothie with a lid, showing the Dunkin’ Donuts logo and the word “Smoothie” on the sleeve, along with an image of fruit. A narrow white margin borders the poster, and a small line of text along the bottom mentions smoothies with real fruit, vitamin C, and low-fat yogurt, followed by the slogan “AMERICA RUNS ON DUNKIN’.” No people are visible.

A single Pepsi can is centered against a deep blue background with a soft glow around it. The can features the classic red, white, and blue Pepsi globe logo and the word “PEPSI” in bold white letters. Its surface is decorated with abstract blue patterns and shapes. Water splashes and droplets surround the can, suggesting cold refreshment, and a small puddle-like reflection appears below it on the floor. No people are present. At the bottom of the image, a small slogan reads, “every PEPSI refreshes the world,” with the brand name in a rectangular white-on-blue block. The overall composition is clean and focused on the beverage can.

The image is a Burger King advertisement featuring a large, close-up hamburger on a warm red background. The burger has a sesame seed bun, layers of leafy green lettuce, thick tomato slices, white onion rings, pickle slices, bacon, melted cheese, and a grilled beef patty, with juices and sauce visible. Bold white text at the top reads “BURRRGERRR KING.” In the bottom right corner are smaller promotional words in Portuguese, including “SOTAQUE CARIOCA,” along with the Burger King logo and a small silhouette of the Christ the Redeemer statue. No people are visible; the focus is entirely on the detailed, appetizing sandwich and the branding text.

The image is a dark, minimalist advertisement featuring a glowing cup of coffee on the left and bold text on the right. A transparent glass cup filled with espresso emits a bright golden light and sparkling particles rising upward, creating a warm halo. On the right side, large white 3D-style letters say “BUY ME A COFFEE.” In the bottom left corner, a small circular Starbucks Coffee logo appears, and along the bottom edge the slogan reads “STARBUCKS. REAL COFFEE.” The background is uniformly black-brown, emphasizing the luminous drink and typography. No people are visible; the composition focuses on the illuminated beverage and branded messaging.

A bright red Coca‑Cola advertisement fills the frame. On the left, a large circular Coca‑Cola logo appears near the top. Below it, a smiling woman with long dark hair and a white shirt is shown from the chest up. She holds a cold glass bottle of Coca‑Cola in her right hand, which is covered with condensation and ice crystals, emphasizing its chill. Across the right side, large white text reads “perfection,” with smaller Spanish text “perfección helada” beneath it. The phrase “ice cold” appears in bold yellow letters to the right of the bottle. The lower edge of the image is lined with chunky ice cubes, enhancing the cold theme.

The image is a minimalist advertisement featuring a single, realistic strip of cooked bacon centered against a large white background. To the left of the bacon is a short block of red text promoting breakfast sandwiches at Dunkin’ Donuts, mentioning the option of bacon. At the bottom center, the Dunkin’ Donuts logo in orange and pink appears beside the slogan “more than coffee and donuts.” Extremely small gray text below notes that Dunkin’ Deli shops are located within participating Dunkin’ Donuts shops in specific U.S. states, which are listed. There are no people shown. The overall design is clean, with abundant negative space emphasizing the bacon and the brand messaging.

A red poster features three bursts arranged like fireworks, each cleverly formed from numerous golden French fries radiating outward. The fries are crisp-looking, lit to appear three-dimensional, and vary in length, creating a celebratory pattern against the gradient red background that darkens toward the top. There are no people in the image. Centered near the bottom, white text reads “CELEBRATING CANNES CREATIVE MARKETER OF THE YEAR.” Beneath the line of text are two small logos: a white cursive “Leo Burnett” signature on the left and a yellow McDonald’s “M” on the right. The overall layout is clean and minimal, emphasizing the fries-as-fireworks concept and the celebratory message.

The image is an advertisement with a blue background featuring a woman in a bright blue dress holding a silver can of Diet Pepsi. She tilts her head and puckers her lips near the can, which has condensation and a striped red‑white‑blue straw. Her nails and lipstick are red, and she wears small stud earrings. To the right are the Pepsi logo and the words “prueba el gran sabor de diet pepsi,” along with a black‑and‑white oval logo reading “Splenda Marca.” Near the bottom right is another can of Diet Pepsi with lipstick marks, and white text saying “más sexy que nunca.” A small Facebook icon and “pepsipr” appear at the bottom.

A promotional poster features a white fabric panel covered with small coffee beans arranged as raised Braille dots. At bottom left of the panel, brown text in Portuguese reads “Novos cardápios em braille Starbucks,” and at the lower right is the green Starbucks siren logo. To the right, the headline “Coffee Braille” appears with sections labeled “Challenge” and “Solution,” describing the use of actual coffee beans to communicate new Braille menus. Three smaller photos show details: a close-up of beans forming Braille, a man pointing toward the bean-studded panel on a wall inside a café, and a hand touching the Braille beans. The layout is clean with generous white space and brown-green brand colors.

A promotional image shows a close-up of a hamburger with a black, sesame‑seed bun on a dark wooden surface against a black background. The burger includes leafy green lettuce, two tomato slices, white onion rings, melted yellow cheese, and a beef patty, with sauce visible near the cheese. The top and bottom buns are both black. To the right, two bottles labeled “A1” lie on their sides, one open with sauce pooled near the mouth. Large text on the right reads “HALLOWEEN WHOPPER” with “A.1 FLAVOR BAKED INTO THE BUN,” styled in bold white letters with some red accents. The lighting highlights the burger’s textures while the surroundings remain shadowed.

The image is a Coca‑Cola advertisement with a solid red background. Four classic glass bottles stand side by side on the left half of the image, each filled with dark soda and covered in condensation. From left to right, the labels read Coca‑Cola in red, Coca‑Cola Life in green with “lower calories,” Coca‑Cola Zero in black with “zero calories,” and Diet Coke in silver with “no calories.” On the right half, large white text says “Good things come in fours.” In the lower right corner, smaller text reads “choose happiness” next to small silhouettes of the four bottle types. No people are visible, and the focus is entirely on the branded bottles and slogans.

A minimalist advertisement features a bright red background with a simple visual at the center: four golden French fries arranged as curved bars forming a Wi‑Fi signal icon. The fries decrease in size from top to bottom, suggesting signal strength. There are no people or other objects in the main area, leaving ample empty space around the design. In the lower-right corner appears the yellow McDonald’s “M” logo, next to small text that reads “love free wi-fi” in yellow and white. The overall look is clean and graphic, using strong contrast between the red backdrop and the golden fries to emphasize the playful Wi‑Fi symbol.

A promotional poster features a playful design on a warm yellow background. At the top, bold white and pink lettering reads, “YOU CAN’T PUT A PRICE ON HAPPINESS.” Centered below is a large U.S. quarter with a bite-sized hole through the middle, aligned with a chocolate-frosted donut covered in colorful sprinkles so the coin appears bitten by the donut. The coin shows a profile portrait and the words “UNITED STATES OF AMERICA” and “LIBERTY.” Near the bottom, orange text proclaims, “BUT 25 CENT DONUTS HELP.” Smaller text explains a special offer on October 25th for 25-cent donuts. In the lower-right corner are small icons and the Dunkin’ logo with the tagline “AMERICA RUNS ON DUNKIN’.”

The image is a colorful advertisement for Pepsi featuring a large paper cup filled with iced cola, with bubbles and ice cubes visible at the top. The cup is blue with the red, white, and blue Pepsi globe logo and the word “pepsi” printed vertically. Water droplets cover the cup exterior, suggesting coldness. The background is divided diagonally into red on the upper left and blue on the lower right, with a white curved band between them. Splashes and fizzing droplets extend across the background near the cup’s rim. Large white text on the right reads “ENJOY A PEPSI,” and smaller white text at the bottom says “LIVE FOR NOW” with the Pepsi globe replacing the letter O. No people appear.

The image is a Starbucks advertisement showcasing seasonal blends. It is divided into four quadrants, each featuring a clear glass mug filled with a different creamy coffee drink topped with whipped cream or caramel. The top-left mug has whipped cream swirled with caramel drizzle; the top-right shows whipped cream sprinkled with small chocolate chips. At the bottom-left, a latte has a crosshatched caramel pattern on the surface, with caramel candies beside the mug. The bottom-right drink is a light-brown latte crowned with a tall swirl of whipped cream dusted with spice. In the center band, the green Starbucks siren logo appears with white text reading “The perfect blend for your favorite show… …and any other occasion.” No people are visible.

The image shows a minimalist scene with five stylized clay cows stacked vertically like an acrobatic tower in the center left of a pale gray background. Each cow has black-and-white patches, pink snouts, small horns, and orange hooves, and they wear small red scarves. Their poses vary—some raise a foreleg, one holds a tail outward, and several appear to strain or wobble, giving the stack a playful, precarious look. The glossy floor beneath them reflects the figures lightly. Near the lower right corner sits a small clay emblem resembling a fast-food logo with blue and orange colors, and beside it the words “BK STICKER” crafted from clay letters. No people are present.

A digital tabletop interface for an Uno card game is displayed on a wooden background. Four circular avatars labeled Player 0, Player 1, Player 2, and Player 3 are positioned around the edges, each tagged “UNORULEAGENT,” with face-down hands showing “+4” above the card backs for players 1–3. At the center, a small panel shows “Direction 1,” a “Deck Size” stack with “+76,” and two red cards: “Played Cards RED 4” and “Target Card RED 4.” At the bottom, Player 0’s visible hand shows seven cards: green 7, yellow 4, blue 1, blue Reverse, yellow Reverse, Wild Draw 4, and green card back labeled GREEN. The word “UNO” is branded across the tabletop.

Player 0’s hand is visible at the bottom, showing cards: green 7, blue 1, yellow 0, a Wild Draw 4, and a green Reverse. Four circular avatars labeled Player 0, Player 1, Player 2, and Player 3 sit around the table, each marked “UNORULEAGENT.” Player 0’s hand is visible at the bottom with five cards: blue 1, yellow Reverse, yellow 9, black Wild Draw 4, and green Reverse. At center left a “Played Cards” row displays previous cards: red 4, yellow 4, then a sequence of green cards 4, 3, 7, 7, 2, 6, followed by two black wild cards stacked. The “Target Card” area at center right shows two black wild cards. A deck stack indicates +76. Hand size boxes for Players 1–3 show face-down cards with +2 each. The word UNO is printed on the table.

Four players are arranged around the screen: Player 0 at the bottom with a visible hand, Player 1 on the left, Player 2 at the top, and Player 3 on the right, each represented by a generic profile icon and a label reading UNORULEAGENT. Player 0’s hand displays four cards: Blue 1, Yellow Reverse, Blue 0, and a black Wild Draw 4.
